previous_subtask_patterns: ^pick up the (?:(?:first|second|third|fourth|fifth) )?(?:red|green|blue) cube(?: at <[0-9]+, [0-9]+>)?(?: for the (?:first|second|third|fourth|fifth) time)?$
success_conditions: The requested-color cube is visibly retained between the fingers and moves with the gripper across current frames.
The cube is visibly clear of its prior support; for PickXtimes the pickup command must provide physical lift margin before placement.
Contact, occlusion, a closed gripper, or motion of the gripper alone is not a verified pickup.
insufficient_evidence: The cube remains supported by the table or target.
The gripper closed near the cube but the cube is not visibly moving with it.
The visible held cube has the wrong color.

required_checks.question: Is the requested-color cube visibly retained between the fingers and moving with the gripper?
Is the cube visibly clear of its previous table or target support rather than merely contacted or occluded?

previous_subtask_patterns: ^place the (?:red|green|blue) cube onto the target(?: at <[0-9]+, [0-9]+>)?$
success_conditions: The same cube from the verified pickup is no longer held and is visibly supported by the designated target.

For only the first repetition, the released pi0.5 place skill may perform the integrated pickup, lift, and release because the frozen initial top-5 vocabulary does not always expose a same-color first-pickup template.
A completed repetition is one ordered pickup/lift then target-release event; prose count claims alone provide no credit.
insufficient_evidence: The cube remains airborne or in the fingers.
The cube was lowered but is not visibly supported by the target.
There was no verified pickup/lift event for this repetition, except inside the single integrated first-place skill.

required_checks.question: Is the cube visibly no longer held, with open separated fingers?
Is that cube visibly resting on the designated target after the verified lift?

success_conditions: The same requested-color cube from the verified pickup crosses into the bin interior and is released there.
The gripper is visibly empty after release; the dark bin interior alone is not used to recount all contents.
The grounded bin point is inside the bin opening and not on the adjacent stop button.
insufficient_evidence: No cube was verified held before the put command.
The cube remains in the gripper, lands outside the bin, or the release location is occluded without a visible crossing event.
The point or gripper trajectory is centered on the stop button rather than the bin opening.

required_checks.question: Did the verified held cube visibly cross the bin rim into its interior?
Is the gripper now visibly empty after releasing that cube inside the bin?
Is the bin grounding visibly inside the dark bin opening and distinct from the nearby gray stop button?
